life_summary: Nathan Eldon Tanner was born May 11, 1898, in Salt Lake City, Utah, into an influential Latter-day Saint family. He developed a distinguished career in business and finance, becoming known for his sharp administrative mind and ethical principles. Tanner earned advanced education and worked as an accountant and business executive, holding leadership positions in various corporate and civic organizations. He married Sara Isabelle Johnson in 1920, and together they built a family centered on church principles and community service. Tanner's background in finance and business administration made him invaluable to church leadership seeking professional management of institutional resources.
church_summary: Tanner served as an Assistant to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles starting in 1942 and was ordained as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve in 1956. He became Second Counselor in the First Presidency in 1960 and served in that position for nearly twenty years, managing the church's temporal affairs with noted efficiency. Tanner was known for his emphasis on financial honesty, prudent resource management, and the principle of paying tithes and offerings to support the church's mission. He helped establish the church's international growth initiatives and served as a trusted advisor to multiple church presidents. His ministry focused on helping members understand the practical application of gospel principles in their daily financial and family lives.
